title: PermissionFile
description: Permission file that can define a default permission, a set of permissions or a list of inlined permissions.

default.description: The default permission set for the plugin

set.description: A list of permissions sets defined

DefaultPermission.description:
The default permission set of the plugin.

Works similarly to a permission with the "default" identifier.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the permission does. Tauri convention is to use `<h4>` headings in markdown content for Tauri documentation generation purposes.

PermissionSet.description: A set of direct permissions grouped together under a new name.

identifier.description: A unique identifier for the permission.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the permission does.

Permission.description:
Descriptions of explicit privileges of commands.

It can enable commands to be accessible in the frontend of the application.

If the scope is defined it can be used to fine grain control the access of individual or multiple commands.

identifier.description: A unique identifier for the permission.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the permission does. Tauri internal convention is to use `<h4>` headings in markdown content for Tauri documentation generation purposes.

commands.description: Allowed or denied commands when using this permission.

scope.description: Allowed or denied scoped when using this permission.

platforms.description: Target platforms this permission applies. By default all platforms are affected by this permission.

Commands.description:
Allowed and denied commands inside a permission.

If two commands clash inside of `allow` and `deny`, it should be denied by default.

Scopes.description:
An argument for fine grained behavior control of Tauri commands.

It can be of any serde serializable type and is used to allow or prevent certain actions inside a Tauri command. The configured scope is passed to the command and will be enforced by the command implementation.

## Example

```json { "allow": [{ "path": "$HOME/**" }], "deny": [{ "path": "$HOME/secret.txt" }] } ```

allow.description: Data that defines what is allowed by the scope.

deny.description: Data that defines what is denied by the scope. This should be prioritized by validation logic.

oneOf.description:
Default grant for the native-webview plugin: navigate a native webview to an
external URL (`open_url`), evaluate JS inside it (`evaluate_js`), patch its
title / subtitle / message chrome labels (`patch_window_text`), present it
(`show`), hide it while keeping it alive (`hide`), and tear it down
(`dispose`). Each references a hand-authored, richly-described per-command
permission file (`open-url.toml`, `evaluate-js.toml`, `patch-window-text.toml`,
`show.toml`, `hide.toml`, `dispose.toml`) rather than the boilerplate
autogenerated `allow-*` grants.

#### This default permission set includes:

- `open-url`
- `evaluate-js`
- `patch-window-text`
- `show`
- `hide`
- `dispose`

oneOf.description:
Allow disposing the native webview — tearing it down (visible or hidden) and
freeing its resources. Emits the `disposed` channel event. Idempotent —
succeeds as a no-op when nothing exists.
oneOf.markdownDescription:
Allow disposing the native webview — tearing it down (visible or hidden) and
freeing its resources. Emits the `disposed` channel event. Idempotent —
succeeds as a no-op when nothing exists.

oneOf.description:
Allow evaluating caller-supplied JavaScript inside the currently-open native
webview (e.g. the host pushing a `window.__nativeWebviewReceive(...)` bridge
message in). The script is run verbatim and not sandboxed; the call errors if
no native webview is open.
oneOf.markdownDescription:
Allow evaluating caller-supplied JavaScript inside the currently-open native
webview (e.g. the host pushing a `window.__nativeWebviewReceive(...)` bridge
message in). The script is run verbatim and not sandboxed; the call errors if
no native webview is open.

oneOf.description:
Allow hiding the native webview — removing it from view while keeping it alive
and running in the background. Emits the `hidden` channel event. Idempotent —
succeeds as a no-op when nothing is visible. Does NOT free resources; use
`dispose` for that.
oneOf.markdownDescription:
Allow hiding the native webview — removing it from view while keeping it alive
and running in the background. Emits the `hidden` channel event. Idempotent —
succeeds as a no-op when nothing is visible. Does NOT free resources; use
`dispose` for that.

oneOf.description:
Allow ensuring a native web view exists over an external `http(s)` URL and
navigating it there: a `WKWebView` (iOS), `android.webkit.WebView` (Android), or
Tauri child webview (desktop) wrapped in native chrome, with the caller's
document-start script injected on any origin and a `Channel<NativeWebviewEvent>`
carrying message / hidden / disposed events back to the host. Navigation only —
presentation is a separate grant (`show`). Non-`http(s)` schemes are rejected.
oneOf.markdownDescription:
Allow ensuring a native web view exists over an external `http(s)` URL and
navigating it there: a `WKWebView` (iOS), `android.webkit.WebView` (Android), or
Tauri child webview (desktop) wrapped in native chrome, with the caller's
document-start script injected on any origin and a `Channel<NativeWebviewEvent>`
carrying message / hidden / disposed events back to the host. Navigation only —
presentation is a separate grant (`show`). Non-`http(s)` schemes are rejected.

oneOf.description:
Allow patching the native webview chrome's three text labels — title, subtitle, and the
bottom-bar message. Each field is independent: omitted = leave unchanged, empty
string = clear, otherwise set. A no-op (resolving "not set") when no native webview is
open, so the host can push speculatively across the native webview lifecycle.
oneOf.markdownDescription:
Allow patching the native webview chrome's three text labels — title, subtitle, and the
bottom-bar message. Each field is independent: omitted = leave unchanged, empty
string = clear, otherwise set. A no-op (resolving "not set") when no native webview is

oneOf.description:
Allow presenting the native webview — bringing a freshly-created or
previously-hidden instance to the foreground. Visibility only; navigation is the
separate `open_url` grant. Idempotent — succeeds as a no-op when nothing exists
to show.
